patch.value: Phase 2: change identities and history rewriting

A version control system that cannot rewrite history is a snapshot store. This phase gives every commit a change identity that survives rewriting, and adds describe, rebase, squash, split, cherry-pick, revert, reset and restore. Descendants are replayed automatically and every branch and tag pointing into a rewritten range is moved, so a rewrite can never orphan a ref. Every rewrite is one transactional operation-log entry, so undo reverses it whole.

Every commit carries a change id that is preserved across describe, rebase, squash and split; rewriting a commit with descendants replays all of them and moves every affected branch and tag; a conflicting rewrite changes no ref and no working-tree byte; record paths merge per field during replay, never by line; 100 percent line, branch and function coverage

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Implementation and command surface complete: engine/rewrite.ts plus nine verbs (describe, rebase, squash, split, cherry-pick, revert, reset, restore, show) and log --change-ids. 337 tests pass. Change identities survive describe, rebase, squash and split; a cherry-pick deliberately gets a NEW id because it is a second distinct change; descendants are replayed and every branch and tag pointing into a rewritten range moves with it; a conflicting rewrite refuses having changed no ref and no working-tree byte, proven by asserting both refs and the file contents after a forced conflict. Four review-quality fixes made on top of what was generated: the six duplicated conflict-translation arms became one shared planned() helper, because four of the six operations cannot conflict at all and six copies read as though every operation can; topoSort became an iterative depth-first walk with push-time dedupe, replacing a scan-for-progress loop whose no-progress guard was unreachable; an empty split half now reports empty_split instead of being dressed up as a conflict whose remediation told the caller to resolve paths that matched nothing; and the rebase replay threads its previous parent through a variable instead of reading it back out of a list with an unreachable fallback.
